verdicts.reason: A keeps everything on one centred axis, but it puts the headline above the shoe, which reverses the original order. The logo, headline, subline and CTA are all tiny next to an oversized shoe, so hierarchy is lost, and the stack has big empty gaps. B has the same undersized text, plus the logo and the Shop Now button are pushed off to the left while the headline stays centred. The CTA sits above the product with a huge dead band in between, and the bottom is empty, so the layout looks arbitrary.

The two are almost identical: centred logo, headline above an oversized shoe, then a small CTA. Both have the same flaws. The headline, subline and CTA are far too small for the canvas, the shoe dominates over the message, and there are big uneven gaps above and below the product. A is a few pixels tighter, which is not a meaningful difference.

A reverses the original order (headline above the product) and leaves the text and CTA tiny under a dominant shoe, with large empty bands. B restores the original order of logo, shoe, headline, subline, CTA, and groups the text and CTA as a block under the product, which is closer to the original. But B's text and CTA are still badly undersized and roughly 170px of the bottom is dead space.
